1.why: All screens use a clean legible sans-serif with adequate line spacing, though letter spacing appears standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instruction text such as 'Use your bank sign-in details to start MFA enrolment' is sentence case with no italics and no dense paragraphs; only the codes/secrets appear in all-caps.

3.why: All screenshots are desktop-width (approx. 1280px), so readability at a mobile screen size cannot be confirmed, though the single-column card layout is simple.

4.why: Every instruction is a single short plain sentence, e.g. 'Create a test-only secret, then add it manually to your authenticator app.'

5.why: The mobile field shows an example placeholder '+44 7700 900000' and demo credentials are displayed, but the recovery code input has no format example.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than one or two short sentences to proceed; the only dense text is the test-only log panel.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as selectable plain text that can be copied, but there is no dedicated copy button and the instructions say to add the secret 'manually'.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent is offered anywhere; the authenticator step explicitly instructs manual entry of the secret.

9.why: Standard email and password fields are present, but no autofill or password-manager support can be verified from the screenshots.

10.why: Each page has a bold step heading and one prominent blue primary button, though the breadcrumb trail does not highlight the current step.

11.why: Each enrolment step asks for a single action, but the MFA security settings page presents three competing buttons (Generate, Test, Sign out).

12.why: Status banners plainly confirm outcomes, e.g. 'MFA is enabled. Save these one-time codes now.' and 'Recovery code accepted. It cannot be used again.'

13.why: Recovery codes can be regenerated and tested without penalty and errors invite retry, but there are no reveal/hide controls for the password or codes.

14.why: The only observed error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', does not state what the problem is, only vaguely suggests retrying, though it does not blame the user.

15.why: No countdowns, timers, or time-limit warnings appear on any screen, so reading and code entry appear untimed.
